read_sources: canonical Habakkuk coordinates and received literary sequence
not_read: state or completion artifacts for Hab

non_authority_statement: Candidate literary and structural evidence only. Every boundary is LOW and deferred_human_or_external_ai. No theology, canon, authorship, date, historicity, chronology, ethics, identity, fulfillment, preferred witness, preferred reading, preferred translation, source tradition, graph, retrieval, reviewed-gold, or promotion authority.
routing_principle: Prefer the larger coherent speech, oracle, woe, or prayer movement. Complaint-answer dialogue, watchpost/tablet framing, repeated woe formulae, the temple-hush close, prayer superscription, theophanic movement, battle imagery, and trembling-to-confidence closure provide form evidence only.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: superscription and two complaint-answer exchanges ending at the watchpost
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: Speaker shifts organize a sustained dialogical movement.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: tablet vision, arrogant-righteous contrast, and five-woe cycle ending in temple hush
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: The inscribed vision and taunt/woe sequence accumulate toward silence before Yahweh.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: superscribed prayer moving from petition through theophany and battle imagery to trembling confidence
macro_parent_alternatives.preservation_reason: Prayer framing and final musical direction favor preserving the chapter as one lyric parent.

global_hot_zones.issue: Plural imperatives, speaker reference, historical identification, and the force of 1:11 are disputed.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep the announced response together and decide no addressee, chronology, or historical fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: Speaker continuity and the seam between second complaint and watchpost can be represented in more than one way.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep the complaint whole; expose the watchpost as a formal hinge while preserving the larger complaint-watch alternative.

global_hot_zones.issue: Pronouns, the vision's timing, the righteous-by-faith/faithfulness line, and the arrogant-subject transition are translation and interpretation hot zones.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep tablet instruction and contrast together; prefer no lexical, theological, or identity decision.

global_hot_zones.issue: The number, exact endpoints, and internal overlap of the woe sayings can invite atomization.
global_hot_zones.handling: Use repeated woe openings and rhetorical closures as evidence while preserving the entire taunt-song cycle as a parent.

global_hot_zones.issue: The idol critique may be counted as the fifth woe or a distinct conclusion, and 2:20 may stand alone as a temple refrain.
global_hot_zones.handling: Preserve idol contrast and temple hush as one culminating movement with narrower alternatives recorded.

global_hot_zones.issue: Poetic geography, divine-war imagery, verbal forms, Selah placement, and historical allusions resist a single English segmentation.
global_hot_zones.handling: Use the broad theophany-to-battle development; decide no chronology, event identity, source layer, or fulfillment.

global_hot_zones.issue: Syntax, economic imagery, and the final musical subscription allow several stanza and paratext treatments.
global_hot_zones.handling: Keep trembling, waiting, deprivation, rejoicing, empowerment, and musical close together.

units.title: Superscription: the oracle Habakkuk saw
units.deciding_marker: A compact genre-and-vision title precedes the first-person complaint.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging the title with the first complaint.
units.risk: authorship, genre force, vision ontology, and title/body relation

units.title: First complaint: how long amid violence and distorted justice
units.deciding_marker: How-long address and first-person cries develop through violence, failed law, and distorted judgment before the answer's plural summons.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting the lament questions from the law-and-justice consequence.
units.risk: speaker, divine action, law, justice, ethics, and historical setting

units.title: First answer: the astonishing Chaldean advance
units.deciding_marker: Look-and-see imperatives announce a work, then a sustained nation portrait runs through speed, conquest, derision, and the difficult closing turn.
units.rejected_alternative: Detaching 1:11 to settle its subject, guilt, or translation.
units.risk: addressee, nation identity, chronology, violence, providence, translation, and fulfillment

units.title: Second complaint: the net, the nations, and unchecked swallowing
units.literary_form: confessional protest and extended fishing metaphor
units.deciding_marker: Direct address and holy/rock predicates lead into the protest, fish-net image, sacrificial celebration, and closing question.
units.rejected_alternative: Breaking the fishing metaphor into independent moral claims or merging it automatically with the watchpost.
units.risk: divine attributes, textual wording, speaker, evil, nations, violence, and theodicy

units.title: Watchpost: awaiting the answer
units.literary_form: prophetic watch declaration and dialogue hinge
units.deciding_marker: First-person resolve to stand, watch, and await a reply formally pivots from complaint to response.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging the watchpost into either the preceding complaint or the following tablet instruction without preserving its hinge function.
units.risk: prophetic experience, speaker posture, translation, and complaint-answer seam

units.title: Tablet vision and the arrogant-righteous contrast
units.literary_form: inscription commission, waiting oracle, and contrast saying
units.deciding_marker: Write/run instruction and appointed-time assurance lead into the puffed-up versus righteous contrast, then the arrogant appetite portrait sets up the taunt.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating 2:4 as a doctrinal proof text or detaching 2:5 solely to identify its subject.
units.risk: vision timing, pronouns, faith/faithfulness translation, later reuse, subject identity, and theology

units.title: First woe: the plunderer plundered
units.deciding_marker: The shared taunt introduces a woe against accumulated pledges, followed by creditor uprising and reciprocal plunder.
units.rejected_alternative: Separating the taunt introduction from its first woe or detaching the reversal.
units.risk: speaker plurality, historical referent, economics, violence, and retribution

units.title: Second woe: unjust gain and the witnessing house
units.literary_form: woe oracle with personified architectural witnesses
units.deciding_marker: Fresh woe opening targets evil gain and secure height; counsel becomes shame, and stone and beam answer one another.
units.rejected_alternative: Detaching the stone-and-beam witness from the house-building accusation.
units.risk: economic ethics, household identity, metaphor, and judgment

units.title: Third woe: the blood-built city and earth-filled knowledge
units.literary_form: woe oracle, futility declaration, and expansive refrain
units.deciding_marker: Fresh woe opening against blood-built settlement develops into futile labor and closes with the waters-cover-sea comparison.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating 2:14 from the blood-and-futility movement as an independent doctrinal prediction.
units.risk: city identity, violence, nations, divine purpose, knowledge, and fulfillment

units.title: Fourth woe: shaming intoxication and reciprocal exposure
units.deciding_marker: Fresh woe opening links drink, exposure, and shame; the cup turns back upon the perpetrator and Lebanon/creature violence answers the accusation.
units.rejected_alternative: Detaching Lebanon and animal violence from the reciprocal cup movement.
units.risk: sexualized shame, violence, geography, creation, cup metaphor, and retribution

units.title: Fifth woe: mute idols and the temple hush
units.literary_form: idol disputation, woe, contrast, and liturgical hush
units.deciding_marker: Profit questions expose the fashioned teacher, the woe addresses a mute object, and the living-presence contrast culminates in earth-wide silence.
units.rejected_alternative: Isolating 2:20 as a contextless liturgical maxim or separating 2:18 from the fifth woe.
units.risk: idolatry, cult, divine presence, temple identity, worship, and source/form classification

units.title: Prayer superscription
units.deciding_marker: Genre label, prophet name, and musical/form term introduce the lyric prayer before direct petition.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging the superscription into the petition or using its technical term to decide performance history.
units.risk: authorship, liturgical setting, technical-term translation, and paratext status

units.title: Petition for renewed work and mercy
units.deciding_marker: Hearing/fearing confession moves through revive-and-make-known imperatives to the mercy plea before the geographic theophany begins.
units.rejected_alternative: Merging the petition into the theophany or atomizing its parallel pleas.
units.risk: translation, chronology, wrath, mercy, revival, and application

units.title: Theophanic approach from Teman and Paran
units.deciding_marker: Geographic advent opens a sustained manifestation through glory, radiance, plague, measuring, shaking, and trembling tents.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting at Selah or converting geographic and cosmic images into a settled event chronology.
units.risk: theophany, geography, poetry, plague, divine-war imagery, Selah, history, and chronology

units.title: Divine-war questions and historical battle imagery
units.literary_form: divine-war hymn with rhetorical questions and victory movement
units.deciding_marker: River-and-sea questions lead through bow, cosmic upheaval, sun and moon, marching, salvation language, head-wounding, and sea trampling.
units.rejected_alternative: Splitting individual battle images into event identifications or using 3:13 to decide messianic identity and fulfillment.
units.risk: divine-war imagery, creation, Exodus/Joshua resonance, translation, anointed identity, history, violence, and fulfillment

units.title: Trembling, patient confidence, rejoicing, and musical close
units.literary_form: first-person response, conditional confidence hymn, and musical subscription
units.deciding_marker: Bodily trembling and waiting turn through crop-and-flock deprivation to nevertheless-rejoicing, strength/deer-height imagery, and the closing direction to the music leader.
units.rejected_alternative: Detaching the famous rejoicing lines or treating the musical close as disposable without recording the full lyric closure.
units.risk: translation, invasion identity, suffering, providence, application, musical direction, and paratext status
